title: Draft: Qt: Dark Theme support
description:
This implements a dark theme for Wireshark depending on the operating
system and settings

milestone.title: Wireshark release 4.0
milestone.description:
Issues and merge requests for the 4.0.0 release, which is currently unscheduled. Major changes include:

* Dropping support for 32-bit Windows.
* Shipping our Windows and macOS packages with Qt 6.
* Display filter syntax fixes and enhancements.
* Conversation UI updates.
* Various build requirement updates.

notes.body:
added 7 commits
  • 38abdff0...33151dc9 - 5 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • d29291a4 - Qt: Dark Theme support
  • 99761eb6 - Fix colors for packetlist
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/6382/diffs?diff_id=346469007&start_sha=38abdff0191f606b98c98be0e76bd1cbe4a7d743)

The following points have to be fixed before this can be merged:

* Fix PacketList coloring, as the defined coloring_rules have to adapt for the darkmode. Currently an approach is being implemented, where the color values are simply inverted in dark mode. That "feels" too easy and lacking, calculating the difference between background and frontcolor and applying it to the coloring_rules seems to be a better approach. 

* I am currently not planning on touching the coloring_rules per se. The idea is, that the colors are being selected always for a "light" mode theme, and will be "calculated" for the dark mode. That way, we do not have to store them separately and the user has ensurance to be able to switch between both themes. Also, changes to profiles may not require changes, allowing profiles to be kept as-is. 

* FileDialogs are somewhat even trickier coming from Qt. There we most certainly will need plattform-specific code. I will first implement that for Windows / Mac with Linux following behind.

* ~~Detection for DarkThemes. This needs to be plattform specific as it is not implemented in Qt. I have code for Mac and Windows, Linux not so far. Will require some fallback code three, but the current code is not working for me.~~ Detection for Windows is implemented, Max and Linux to follow

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/6382/diffs?diff_id=347649929&start_sha=99761eb69caeda481d804a3269b997c9cf1f5a0e)

I am currently in the process of switching to another stylesheet. https://github.com/ColinDuquesnoy/QDarkStyleSheet to be specific, as it includes both a dark and a light stylesheet and we can switch between those with certainty.

added 1 commit

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/6382/diffs?diff_id=348632634&start_sha=dbcec9a5685b02398124b50da25d23199d17741e)

I tested loading a capture file and opening a few common windows here on Windows 10 21H2, and it looks great!

There are a couple of issues with dropping the native Windows file dialogs: there are lots of Windows utilities that integrate with them (e.g. 7zip), and the Qt dialogs are ugly. I'm not sure if the former is a big concern or not, and we might be able to fix the latter by creating a wrapper class that de-uglifies the dialog, e.g. by using native system icons.

+#include <ui/qt/themes/theme_eventfilter.h>
+
+#ifdef Q_OS_WINDOWS
+#include <Windows.h>
+#endif
+
+ThemeEventFilter::ThemeEventFilter(QObject* parent) : QObject(parent) {}
+
+bool ThemeEventFilter::nativeEventFilter(const QByteArray& eventType, void* message, long*)
+{
+#ifdef Q_OS_LINUX
+    if (eventType == "xcb_generic_event_t") {
+
+    }
+#endif
+#ifdef Q_OS_MAC
+    if (eventType == "mac_generic_NSEvent") {
+
+    }
+#endif
+#ifdef Q_OS_WINDOWS
+#if(_WIN32_WINNT >= 0x0501)
+    LRESULT code = WM_STYLECHANGED;
+    /* Windows 10 in later versions explicitely informs of the color scheme change */
+#if(_WIN32_WINNT >= 0x0600)
+    code = WM_DWMCOLORIZATIONCOLORCHANGED;
+#endif 
+    if (eventType == "windows_generic_MSG") {
+        MSG* msg = (MSG*)message;
+        if (msg->message == code)
+            themeChanged();
+    }
+#endif
+#endif
+
+    return false;
+};
